# MisakaNet
mcp-name: io.github.Ikalus1988/misakanet

> **The same failure, paid for twice.**
>
> A `pip install` times out behind a corporate proxy. An a

gent finds the fix. Days later the same
> timeout appears on another machine, under another model —

and is debugged from scratch, because the
> fix was never written down anywhere the next agent looks

.
>
> MisakaNet is that place: a git-backed **failure memory**. Every lesson is a Markdown file in t

his
> repository — graded by evidence, reviewed like code, retrieved by an agent instead of guessed

at.
> You fail once; the next agent does not.

Agent-native interfaces: MCP server (8 tools), WebMCP, `llms.txt`,
A2A discovery via `.well-known/ag

ent-card.json`. The **local** stdio server (`pip install misakanet`)
ships **11** — the hosted endpo
int is a subset; docs/mcp.md has both rows.

## What is MisakaNet?

**Git-backed failure memory for AI coding agents.** An error shows up → the agent searches → it
appl

ies a fix somebody already verified → if nothing matches, the miss becomes an intake, and the
intake
becomes a lesson for the next agent.
Every lesson is a Markdown file: reviewed like code, graded by evidence, retrieved with BM25 over th

e
Python standard library. The hosted MCP endpoint adds an **optional semantic fallback** (bge-m3 +
Vectorize) only when BM25 returns no match; `MISAKANET_SEMANTIC=0` disables it. No vector database i

s
required locally, and no server unless you want one.

| **Lessons** | failure-recovery knowledge base, open and auditable under `lessons/` |
| **Domains**

| rag · devops · fanuc · docker · feishu · mcp · network · ci · wsl · windows … |

### What it answers — and what it does not
MisakaNet answers for the failures it has indexed, and only those. When nothing matches the reply is
`no_match` plus a ready-to-call `intake` — the corpus saying "not this one yet", not a dead end.
### What changed since: the gate, not the model

## Recitation benchmark: what it measured, and why it is paused

One narrow question: **when you hand a model a lesson, how much of that lesson comes back?** The
met

ric is `lesson_hit_rate` — the share of the injected lesson's commands reproduced in the answer.
Rea
d the setup before the number: the scenario in this benchmark is each lesson's own title, the inject

ed
lesson is *that same lesson*,
no retrieval call is made, and correctness is not checked. It measu

res the **recitation** half of RAG:
necessary for MisakaNet to help, and **not evidence that search

ion** half of RAG:
necessary for MisakaNet to help, and **not evidence that search finds anything**.
The run is **paused**. Two independent runs of ≈500 scenarios each on 2026-09-22: **46.1%** with the

lesson pasted in, **23.3%** without. What remains is the last snapshot plus its dated record —
`doc
s/benchmarks/latest.json`.
